findings.finding: F1: the spec's load command carries no -timeout; -count=40 is one binary against Go's 10-minute default, and the rewritten test runs two cases per iteration (~4.8 s), so ~190 s unloaded and several times that under the prescribed load. The workflow has already gone red on that default (.github/workflows/envoy-and-contracts.yaml:976-978).
findings.answer: The plan's step 4 runs the spec's command with -timeout 30m -v added and says why; recorded as spec departure 2. Every other command in the plan carries an explicit -timeout too, including the whole-package run (~700 s here).

findings.finding: F2: neither named mutation isolates one case. Both redden both new subtests, and both redden TestCreateAskOnProjectDocumentSuggests (suggestions_test.go:466-494), which rides the same suggestions-only branch (asks.go:298-301).
findings.answer: The plan names the full expected red set per mutation, subtest by subtest plus the document test, and runs each mutation over the whole 40-test 'Suggest' set rather than a narrowed -run, with the base measured green (67 s). It also requires the mutation be confirmed applied before its result is read (docs/solutions/testing/a-mutation-that-did-not-apply-produces-a-green-that-is-yours-INFRA-31.md) and restored with jj restore plus an empty jj diff --stat.

findings.finding: F3: 'emptying its suggestions' has two readings; only &model.Suggestions{} reddens the generous case on the answered-question assertion, and today's compound t.Fatalf (suggestions_test.go:373-375) prints one message for three causes, so no run can show which clause fired.
findings.answer: The plan pins mutation A to suggestionsOnlyAdvice{Suggestions: &model.Suggestions{}}, says explicitly why nil is the wrong reading, and requires one clause per t.Fatalf in the rewritten test (missing advice key, null envelope, missing decision, wrong decision id, each with its own message).

findings.finding: F4: the spec's before-run cannot be run on today's tree - writeSuggestionTimeout is an unexported const with no setter, and newFailingAdviceHandler takes only a query name.
findings.answer: Step 1 of the plan lands the seam and the helper parameter first, keeps the old single-case body, points it at the forced allowance and runs -count=5 as the red set before the rewrite. The planner has already run exactly that: 5 failures of 5 at suggestions_test.go:374, message quoted in the plan.

findings.finding: F5: no surface proves the deployment still waits 300 ms. The sibling tests allow writeSuggestionTimeout + 500 ms of wall time, which a default of 10 ms or 290 ms satisfies identically, and neither goes through a route; README and CHANGELOG state the figure in prose only.
findings.answer: The plan adds one database-free pin, TestTheDeploymentsSuggestionAllowanceIsTheDocumentedBound, asserting (&server{}).suggestionAllowance() == 300*time.Millisecond against the literal rather than the constant, with (&server{}) as the package's own production-shape idiom (routes_table_test.go:56,109). The documents' half is checked by their absence from jj diff --stat, which the plan makes part of the evidence.

findings.finding: F6: the spec calls the two sibling tests' passing 'the check that the seam reaches them', but both build their server with directServer(deps) = &server{deps: deps} (server_test.go:207-209), so they run the default path and prove no reach.
findings.answer: The plan leaves them unedited, records their green as no-regression evidence, and names the forced subtest - which drives the accessor through the ask route - as the reach proof. Recorded as spec departure 1 so the architect can decide whether the spec's sentence changes.

findings.finding: F7: the forced case never reaches the leg that failed in the wild. The ask route passes an empty project, so a 1 ns allowance ends the step at resolveSuggestionProject; the measured failure was the later shape (related populated, decision nil, record then lost), which after the change no test asserts.
findings.answer: Confirmed by the planner's own run: Missing reads 'the project lookup behind it did not answer within 1ns' and Related is empty. The plan records it under 'What this does not cover' and requires it on the pull request's Not proven / risk line. The only deterministic route to the middle state is the sibling tests' table-lock technique, which the spec does not ask for and the architect's boundary excludes.

findings.finding: F8: asserting Decision == nil in the forced case is also what an empty corpus produces, so it can be green for the wrong reason; dropping it with minimal seeding would halve the per-iteration cost.
findings.answer: The plan keeps the full seeding in both cases and keeps the assertion, because the generous case is the positive control over the identically seeded corpus - the measured cost is 2.4 s per iteration, the same as today's single case, so the saving was not worth the weaker assertion. The subtest's comment records why trimming the seeding would break it.

findings.finding: F9 [INFERENCE in the analysis]: the forced case's determinism rests on pgx refusing an already-expired context, which the analyst could not read in this tree.
findings.answer: Measured rather than inferred: 5 failures of 5 at 1 ns in this pod, every one carrying the envelope with Missing set and Decision absent. The plan also forbids asserting the text of Missing, since it interpolates the forced value.

findings.finding: F10: evidence the spec requires that the sketch did not list - each result naming its command, runs and failure messages; pass and fail counts, busy-loop count and wall seconds per run; the repository's exact load recipe; a run of the whole suggestion set; and the branch's own CI runs.
findings.answer: The plan's seven ordered steps name each run as a deliverable, state that pass/fail counts come from counting --- PASS:/--- FAIL: subtest lines under -v (a bare ok is not evidence, since a test skips and reports success when DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset, storetest.go:60), fix the load recipe at two busy loops plus the dd writer with a trap, and require the branch's envoy-go and envoy-go-race runs quoted by run id and state after the push.

findings.finding: F11: the second Missing interpolation lives in computeSuggestions (suggestions.go:170), a separate method, and the repository requires no CHANGELOG entry or docs/solutions entry for this change.
findings.answer: The plan names all three constant uses to move (suggestions.go:119, :126, :170), notes that computeSuggestions is a method on the same *server so it calls the accessor directly with no new parameter, and states that CHANGELOG.md and README.md stay out of the diff - their absence from jj diff --stat being part of the evidence - with docs/solutions left to retro.

findings.finding: F12: a third positional parameter on newFailingAdviceHandler diverges from the package's testServerOptions idiom, and a server-field seam is unreachable from any handler built through newTestServer/register.
findings.answer: The plan keeps the positional parameter and says why: zero-means-the-default is how this package already spells an optional test timeout (DepsInput.EnvoyTimeout, server.go:127-129), two call sites pass 0, and newFailingAdviceHandler already hand-builds its &server{} literal. The server field is deliberately unreachable from register - that is what keeps the README's and the changelog's 300 ms unconditional, which an exported Deps knob would not.

specDepartures.spec: The two sibling deadline tests 'must still pass against whatever the change makes the allowance, which is the check that the seam reaches them.'
specDepartures.plan: The plan leaves both tests unedited and treats their passing as no-regression evidence only; the proof that the seam is reached is the forced subtest, which drives the new accessor through POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/asks.
specDepartures.evidence: Both tests build their server with directServer(deps), which is &server{deps: deps} (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/server_test.go:207-209), so the new suggestionTimeout field is zero and they exercise the default path. Routing their bound through the accessor instead would force the const bound expressions at suggestions_test.go:289 and :325 to become vars and would edit two tests the spec leaves alone.

acceptance: The criterion 'the two sibling tests must still pass, which is the check that the seam reaches them' becomes two: the siblings stay green unedited (no regression), and the forced subtest is the seam-reach proof.

specDepartures.spec: 'go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run TestCreateAskOnIssueKeepsSuggestionsWhenWriteAdviceFails -count=40', with one busy loop per processor and a looping disk writer beside it at low priority, passes with no failure of any kind.
specDepartures.plan: The same command with -timeout 30m -v added, its result read as 80 passing subtest lines and no failure.
specDepartures.evidence: -count=40 is one test binary against Go's undeclared 10-minute default. The rewritten test runs two cases per iteration at about 2.4 s each (measured in this pod on 2026-10-24), so roughly 190 s unloaded and several times that under the prescribed load; the same default already took this workflow red once (.github/workflows/envoy-and-contracts.yaml:976-978). -v is needed because the pass and fail counts the spec asks for cannot be read from a single ok line.

acceptance: The load criterion's command gains -timeout 30m -v; its verdict becomes 80 passing subtest lines and zero failures, recorded with busy=2, the wall seconds and the gVisor loadavg note.
